title: The Design and Implementation of an Educational Chatbot with Personalized Adaptive Learning Features for Project Management Training
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how educational chatbots can be designed using personalized adaptive learning (PAL) principles for project management training in higher education. The authors note that prior educational chatbot research has largely focused on STEM and language learning, with little work in multidisciplinary fields such as project management, and even less on chatbots that combine personalization, adaptivity, and generative AI. They therefore ask how an educational chatbot can be designed utilizing PAL for project management training.

To answer this, the paper presents PMTutor, a chatbot built using design science research. PMTutor combines rule-based dialog logic, natural language understanding, and an OpenAI GPT-3 service, and it includes five PAL features: self-assessment, topic recommendation, tailored exercise feedback for correct/incorrect answers, the ability to resume or review exercises, and answering learner questions. Content was designed by teaching staff and domain experts using a topic configuration template, and the system was piloted in project management courses.

The main empirical context was a one-and-a-half-hour online pilot in a Finnish postgraduate project management course, with 30 students participating and 29 completing retrospective pre/post self-assessments. The study also incorporated student feedback from open-ended survey responses and earlier testing workshops used during development. Results suggest that PMTutor can complement learning, provide engaging interactive exercises, and support learners through immediate customized feedback. Participants particularly valued the exercise feedback, though they also reported usability issues such as language mismatch and navigation difficulties. The authors conclude that PAL chatbots can support project management learning, but they emphasize the need for stronger usability testing, incremental design, and further development of generative-AI-supported personalized interaction.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot/LLM system for natural-language question answering and response generation.
identified_tools.use_case: Used via OpenAI GPT-3 (text-davinci-003) to answer learner questions beyond the scope of PMTutor's NLU and dialog logic.

findings.finding_summary: In the pilot, PMTutor's GPT-3-backed question-answering feature was perceived as useful by some learners, with 1 respondent in the UX analysis explicitly noting the ability to answer open questions as positive. However, 2 respondents also reported that PMTutor did not adequately answer their open questions, indicating mixed user experience rather than a clear learning gain attributable to the LLM feature.
findings.measure: Qualitative survey feedback on user experience and ability to answer open questions

identified_tools.name: PMTutor
identified_tools.description: An educational chatbot system for project management training that combines rule-based dialogue, NLU, and an LLM service to provide interactive exercises, adaptive topic recommendations, self-assessment, resumable exercises, and question answering.
identified_tools.use_case: Designed and piloted as a minimum viable personalized adaptive learning chatbot integrated into a project management course for postgraduate students.

findings.finding_summary: Among 30 postgraduate students, 25 provided positive UX feedback and 16 said PMTutor was moderately to very helpful in achieving the learning objective 'I can calculate a project's schedule and critical path using an activity network.' Retrospective self-assessment on activity network competence increased from median 3 to 4 among n=29, with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test showing the increase was statistically significant (Z = -4.354, p = 0.0000134).
findings.measure: Retrospective pre/post self-assessment of activity network competence; qualitative feedback on user experience and learning outcome

quality_tier_rationale: This is a single mixed-methods pilot with survey and thematic analysis rather than a controlled experimental design. The evidence is useful but limited by the small sample and reliance on self-report.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports a statistically significant improvement in retrospective self-assessment, but no standardized effect size is provided and the outcome is self-reported competence. The practical impact appears promising yet modest and preliminary.
